pages.name: CASE STUDY INTRODUCTION
pages.title: OODI SMART BUILDING INTELLIGENCE
pages.subtitle: Public building data, weather context and conceptual intelligence layers translated into a clear Digital Advisory experience.
pages.paragraph1: This self-initiated case study explores how public utility data, current weather context and clearly labelled conceptual building-intelligence modules can be transformed into an accessible digital experience for decision-makers and stakeholders.
pages.paragraph2: Bringing together public data and conceptual intelligence layers to communicate resource use, spatial context, data quality and building-performance information.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: PROJECT CHALLENGE
pages.title: FROM FRAGMENTED DATA TO A CLEAR BUILDING STORY
pages.subtitle: Public building data may be technically available while remaining difficult to interpret, compare and communicate.
pages.paragraph1: Utility readings, timestamps, weather context and spatial information often exist in separate systems. The challenge was to organize these sources into one understandable experience without overstating data quality or operational capability.
pages.paragraph2: Create an executive and stakeholder-facing interface that connects building identity, resource performance, spatial context and transparent data provenance.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW
pages.title: A CONNECTED VIEW OF BUILDING PERFORMANCE
pages.subtitle: A single interface brings together building context, public utility readings, current weather and high-level observations.
pages.paragraph1: The Overview experience presents electricity, heat, water and district cooling independently, while preserving their source, timestamp, unit and availability status.
pages.paragraph2: Resource summaries, weather context, deterministic observations and data classifications are presented in a format suitable for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: RESOURCE PERFORMANCE
pages.title: UTILITY-AWARE RESOURCE PERFORMANCE
pages.subtitle: Electricity, heat, water and district cooling respond through synchronized visual and analytical states.
pages.paragraph1: Selecting a resource updates the architectural overlay, chart, KPIs, timestamps, unit and data-quality status. Requested and effective periods remain visible so fallback data is never presented as current.
pages.paragraph2: The experience preserves independent utility timestamps, supports multiple time windows and does not interpolate or fabricate unavailable readings.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: BUILDING INTELLIGENCE
pages.title: BUILDING INTELLIGENCE THROUGH SPATIAL STORYTELLING
pages.subtitle: Conceptual zones and intelligence layers demonstrate how operational information could be communicated spatially.
pages.paragraph1: Users can explore four building levels and five intelligence layers, including occupancy, indoor comfort, air quality, HVAC and asset health.
pages.paragraph2: All spatial indicators are deterministic prototype content. They are clearly separated from public building data and do not imply a connection to real sensors, BMS platforms or operational controls.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: INSIGHTS
pages.title: DETERMINISTIC INSIGHTS WITHOUT UNSUPPORTED CLAIMS
pages.subtitle: The Insights experience converts available data and coverage conditions into concise observations.
pages.paragraph1: Priority notices, latest readings, weather context and data-quality information are generated through deterministic rules rather than a language model.
pages.paragraph2: The interface avoids unsupported causal conclusions, forecasts and synthetic performance scores. Partial or unavailable periods remain explicitly labelled.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: DATA TRANSPARENCY
pages.title: CLEAR DISTINCTION BETWEEN REAL AND CONCEPTUAL DATA
pages.subtitle: The methodology page explains the origin, timing, limitations and classification of every information layer.
pages.paragraph1: Nuuka provides public property-level utility data. Open-Meteo provides current public weather context. The Building Intelligence dataset is deterministic conceptual prototype content.
pages.paragraph2: The application documents fallback behavior, cached snapshots, partial coverage, independent timestamps, image attribution and project limitations.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.

pages.name: ROLE AND TECHNOLOGY
pages.title: FROM PRODUCT CONCEPT TO DEPLOYED MVP
pages.subtitle: A complete self-initiated case study spanning strategy, UX/UI, public APIs, technical visualization, testing and deployment.
pages.paragraph1: The project was developed as a browser-based Digital Advisory prototype with a strong focus on data integrity, accessible communication and portfolio-quality presentation.
pages.paragraph2: Product strategy, information architecture, UX/UI direction, data-source evaluation, technical visualization, AI-assisted development, QA and portfolio packaging. ChatGPT, Claude Code and Codex were development-assistance tools only; no generative AI runs inside the deployed application.
pages.disclaimer: Independent portfolio prototype using public data and clearly labelled conceptual layers.
